doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Fletcher Henderson's orchestra at a Veterans' Building dance
summary: Performing in a WPA skit as a child, he hears the Fletcher Henderson orchestra without knowing who they were.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yes. Uh huh. And anyhow but in the meantime I’m down there watching all the drummers. Every time something would happen — as a matter of fact, going way back, before I became interested, back in the early thirties, it was during the depression, and not only did we have the Music Project but you had another project where they would send people, show business people, people that had stage experience, and they would send them around to the neighborhoods and I remember the house, there was a house on Sacramento Street with a large, it was a Victorian with a large dining room/living room. And so they would send this team out, a man and woman team out, and we teenagers would go up there and they’d teach us routines. We had the School Days routine, then we had another routine that we did, and then you’d rehearse and then you’d perform. So we had lines to speak and we had little dance routines, and also the Music Project would send a pianist to do that playing. And anyhow one of the times when our black veterans of war — the American Legion — they gave a program at the Veteran’s Building here, the War Memorial building. And so the program was we youngsters, we’d do our skit and

then there would be a dance after that. So we did our skit and then the band, they were already set up and they came from the dressing room or wherever they were and they started to play for the dancing. It turned out to be the Fletcher Henderson orchestra. And now what am I, twelve years old? Thirteen years old? Something like that. Here’s the Fletcher Henderson orchestra. Now the drummer’s name was Pete Suggs — S-U-G-G-S. And I’ve seen his name on some of the personnel on some of the older records now. I don’t know whether Roy and Ben Webster — Roy Eldridge and Ben Webster — were on that band or not, because I didn’t know at that time. But they were with him. They were with Fletcher Henderson.
Now did you know who the Fletcher Henderson orchestra was at that time?
